aspects.says: A packager borrowed from a BCD link with only its text fields switched to EBCDIC still sends a BCD MTI the host can't read.
basis: section:6.1. A Mastercard Message Is EBCDIC Characters Behind a Binary Bitmap

aspects.says: Mastercard's clearing files are described as 1993-edition messages, unlike the 1987 online authorizations.
basis: section:6.1. A Mastercard Message Is EBCDIC Characters Behind a Binary Bitmap
aspects.reason: a hedged side note about a confidential file format, which nothing offline can check

aspects.says: On a Mastercard-style link the MTI, numbers, length prefixes and text are one EBCDIC byte each and only the bitmap is binary, so a BCD packager's MTI can't be read.
basis: section:6.1. A Mastercard Message Is EBCDIC Characters Behind a Binary Bitmap

aspects.says: Field 48 is an optional category code then tag-length-value subelements, found by walking lengths, never at fixed offsets or by searching for the tag's digits.
basis: section:6.4. Field 48 Is Read Tag by Tag, and an Unknown Tag Must Not Stop the Message

aspects.says: PostChannel in a ChannelAdaptor descriptor frames a Mastercard-style link in Q2.
basis: section:6.3. A Frame Is a Two-Byte Binary Length, Then the Message
aspects.reason: deploying a live channel needs a network host; the framing it produces is checked by the quiz

aspects.says: A wrong field class packs and unpacks its own bytes, so only a comparison with the specification's sample bytes catches it.
basis: section:6.2. A Packager That Reads Its Own Messages Back Proves Nothing

aspects.says: The frame is a two-byte binary length and the message; a binary-length host reading ASCII digits waits for 12336 bytes until its read timeout.
basis: section:6.3. A Frame Is a Two-Byte Binary Length, Then the Message

aspects.says: jPOS's subfield packager refuses a tag it has no definition for, and the whole message with it, so every tag is declared or the field is split in code.
basis: section:6.4. Field 48 Is Read Tag by Tag, and an Unknown Tag Must Not Stop the Message
